concerns.text: The plan defines the target variable CAPE as a deterministic function of unit_cell_volume and atomic vdW volumes (FR-011). The predictors include 3D geometric descriptors (radius_of_gyration, asphericity) derived from the SAME 3D coordinates used to calculate the unit cell volume and atomic positions. This creates a circular validation: the model predicts a metric (CAPE) using features (3D geometry) that are definitionally coupled to the components of that metric. The 'predictive' relationship is largely tautological (geometry predicts geometry) rather than testing if SMILES topology predicts packing.

The definition of CAPE normalizes Packing Coefficient by average atomic volume. The predictors include 'atom_count' and 'atom_type_counts'. Since the denominator of CAPE is explicitly a function of atom counts and types, the model is trained to predict a value that is mathematically constrained by its own inputs. This violates the independence of predictors and outcome, rendering the correlation coefficient (r) a measure of mathematical identity rather than empirical predictive power.

The plan proposes a partial correlation analysis to 'disentangle compositional vs. geometric effects' (FR-014). However, since the target (CAPE) is constructed from the very compositional and geometric variables being controlled for, the partial correlation will be statistically unstable and conceptually flawed. You cannot control for the variables that define the target to prove the target isn't just those variables; the analysis is circular by design.
